answer: When an AI agent wants to act in the economy, it must post a bond that a single human or wallet cannot spread across many pseudonyms. Registrations are clustered by shared funding, timing, and attested device, so a farm of fresh identities gets merged into one stake. The bond therefore acts as an anchor: each real operator reaches a safe inlet of cheap identity, but a Sybil swarm must lock capital for every fake seat it claims, and the cost lands at its nadir only after it has already burned funds it cannot recover.
